articles.title: Chelsea change course with Alonso primed to banish the chaos of youth
articles.summary: The 44-year-old is focused on maintaining ‘emotional control’ and a slew of sensible signings offer genuine hope. It is a necessary reset. Although it would be pushing it to say that Chelsea have switched from development centre to retirement home, even after the signings of Jordan Henderson and…
body: Discipline was a problem for Chelsea last season: they had 11 red cards in all competitions and a lot of the wounds were self-inflicted. Chelsea were impetuous, on the receiving end of too many bookings for dissent and prone to collapsing at the first sign of trouble. No wonder Alonso, who was the epitome of calm during his playing career, has focused on maintaining “emotional control” before opening his tenure as manager with Monday’s trip to Fulham.

It will be a test of Chelsea’s mentality. Craven Cottage has been the setting for some spectacular implosions during the BlueCo era, the path to two 2-1 victories for Fulham over their neighbours smoothed by João Félix earning a red card on his Chelsea debut in 2023 and by Marc Cucurella getting himself sent off after 22 minutes last season.

Chelsea need to change, and hiring Alonso was a tacit admission that their approach required fine-tuning. Internally there was a recognition that the club had undervalued the importance of aura when it came to hiring coaches.

articles.title: Rising star Yamashita ties LPGA scoring record
articles.summary: Rising star Miyu Yamashita ties an LPGA Tour scoring record as she surges to a dominant nine-shot victory at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada.
body: The 25-year-old from Japan made an eight-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole to complete a four-under 66 on Sunday and finish the week on a 23-under 257.
It matched Kim Sei-young 72-hole tour record lowest total, with the South Korean also carding 257 when finishing 31 under at Thornberry Creek in 2018.
Yamashita broke the tournament's record of 262, set by South Korea's Ko Jin-young in 2019.
Having dominated from the opening round, Yamashita headed into the final day with a six-shot lead and extended that with six birdies in a closing four-under 66 on the Royal Mayfair course.

articles.title: Big decisions pay off as Coco Gauff gears up for US Open with Cincinnati title
articles.summary: American beats compatriot Jessica Pegula 6-2, 6-4. Gauff claims first title of season, second in Cincinnati. One year ago, Coco Gauff departed the Cincinnati Open with her career at a crossroads.
body: It has taken an enormous amount of resilience, patience and toil, but this week Gauff began to feel the consequences of those efforts as she closed out one of the smoothest tournaments of her career with her best performance of the season, thoroughly outplaying the third seed Jessica Pegula to win 6-2, 6-4 and clinch the Cincinnati Open title for the second time in her career.

This tournament marked Gauff’s fifth WTA 1000 semi-final of the season and her third final. Gauff has enjoyed a fairly consistent past five months on the tour but the 22-year-old had yet to finish any tournament this season without a defeat. Victory in Cincinnati marks her first title of the season and fourth career WTA 1000 title.

articles.title: Banned Sydney Swans players not welcome at Brownlows as AFL delays inquiry until police probe concludes
articles.summary: AFL chief executive Andrew Dillon faces media for first time since players stood down, saying ‘the way we treat women says a lot about who we are’ The AFL will not invite five Sydney Swans players suspended by their club to this year’s Brownlow medal ceremony, as the league holds fire on opening…
body: The AFL’s chief executive, Andrew Dillon, faced the media on Monday for the first time since Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon were stood down for the rest of the AFL season by the Swans tfor breaching the club’s standards, including drinking and bringing women back to their hotel.

Victoria police are separately continuing to investigate an alleged sexual assault early on Monday morning at the Pullman Hotel, where the Swans were staying after beating Essendon at the MCG last Sunday. No one has been arrested or charged and the five players have reportedly denied any criminal wrongdoing.
Dillon said the AFL “cannot get in the way of a police investigation”.

“There’s a police investigation going on now,” Dillon said the launch of this year’s AFL finals on Monday. “Once that’s complete, we’ll conduct our own inquiries. But the AFL won’t get involved while there’s a police investigation under way.

articles.title: Scott's World title aim after testing personal period
articles.summary: Olympic champion Hannah Scott is preparing for the World Championships in Amsterdam which begin on Tuesday after her "most successful winter of training so far".
body: The Coleraine sculler says her experience to date in the sport is becoming "more and more useful, which is even showing across the team".
Scott won Olympic gold in Paris two years ago but her story has been a rollercoaster ride of injury and illness as well as success and joy.
On the water, life is good, and the public will get to see that this week as Scott and her team-mates compete in the Netherlands.
But, away from competition, elite athletes like Scott face the same challenges as anyone else and she has opened up about some of the issues she has had to navigate recently.

articles.title: Arbeloa v Alonso: Benitez on his former players turned managers
articles.summary: Former Liverpool manager Rafael Benitez on his former players Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa who face each other as managers on Monday when Fulham host Chelsea.
body: When former Liverpool manager Rafael Benitez is asked whether he had expected his then-players Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa to become managers, his response is brutally honest.
"Alonso, yes. Arbeloa, not really," he says. "For me, Arbeloa was a surprise."
Almost 20 years after Benitez brought them together at Anfield, the pair will go head-to-head as Arbeloa's Fulham host Alonso's Chelsea on Monday.
The pair won the 2010 World Cup and two European Championships with Spain, along with domestic league and cup triumphs when they both joined Real Madrid after Liverpool.

articles.title: Maradona's 'Hand of God' ball sells for £2.5m
articles.summary: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous 'hand of God' goal in the 1986 World Cup quarter-final victory over England is sold at auction.
body: Maradona famously punched the ball past goalkeeper Peter Shilton in Argentina's 2-1 quarter-final win over England.
After the game, he told reporters it had been scored "a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God".
Maradona later scored what became known as the 'goal of the century' in the same game, dribbling past five England outfield players before slotting the ball past Shilton.
Though it sold for $3.3m (£2.5m) at Heritage Auctions in the United States on Saturday, the ball had been expected to fetch nearer $10m (£7.3m).

articles.title: Sri Lanka vs India 2nd Test live win probability, scorecard, chances of victory in Colombo
articles.summary: Track Sri Lanka vs India 2nd Test live win probability, full scorecard, updates, and real-time victory chances from the SSC Ground in Colombo.
body: The India-Sri Lanka series shifts venues for its decider, moving from Galle's spin-friendly track to the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo, which is a ground known for offering a very different kind of contest.
Batting first has historically paid off at this venue, with teams regularly posting big totals early in matches, which makes Wednesday's toss potentially decisive.

Rain looms as a genuine concern too, with forecasts suggesting interruptions across all five days, while Colombo's heat is expected to sap energy from the bowling attacks. Spin has still had the upper hand recently, as spinners have picked up 45 wickets across the last three Tests here, compared to 35 for the pacers.

India arrive full of confidence following their commanding 165-run win in the series opener. Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul, and Manav Suthar were the standout contributors in Galle. They will fancy their chances of completing a 2-0 sweep, a result that would also strengthen their push toward the 2027 World Test Championship final.

articles.title: Meet the Filipino tennis superstar-in-waiting with a punch to rival Pacquiao's
articles.summary: "Once it grows, it cannot be stopped" - tennis superstar-in-the-making Alex Eala is quickly becoming the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao.
body: The 21-year-old is carrying the hopes of a nation, the volume of support when she plays calling to mind the days when world boxing champion 'Pac Man' put the country on the map as a sporting force.

Few young players on the WTA Tour have experienced the level of expectation and support Eala has received ‌since she earned a place on the circuit, and she showed what all the fuss is about ‌by winning the recent Washington Open.

After a run to the fourth round of Wimbledon, which included a victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek, Eala capped her breakthrough in the US capital by rallying to defeat top seed Jessica Pegula 4-6 ​6-4 6-0 in a rain-interrupted final, becoming the first woman from her country to claim a tour-level singles crown.
Along the way, ​she beat Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, last year's winner Leylah ‌Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka.

articles.title: 'It makes me feel uncomfortable' - is Martinelli being frozen out?
articles.summary: Arsenal have held talks with Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal over the sale of winger Gabriel Martinelli. The Brazil international is free to leave the club this summer, with manager Mikel Arteta making it clear to the attacker that he is not in his plans.
body: Turkish club Galatasaray showed interest in Martinelli earlier this summer, but the Brazilian would not consider a move to Istanbul, despite Arsenal receiving a 45m euro (£38.54m) bid.
As reported by BBC Sport's senior football correspondent Sami Mokbel, Al-Hilal have communicated that they are willing to bid higher than Galatasaray's offer.
Martinelli made 53 appearances last season, scoring 11 goals, but he was left out of the squad for the champions Premier League opener against Coventry City on Friday.
"The way Martinelli is being treated at the moment, it really makes me feel uncomfortable," former Arsenal striker Ian Wright told Sky Sports.

articles.title: Nev on title race: Liverpool, Man City nowhere near levels required
articles.summary: Liverpool and Manchester City are well below the level required to win the Premier League title this season, says Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville.
body: City are entering the unknown after Pep Guardiola's departure, while Liverpool are rebuilding under Andoni Iraola.
A last-gasp Josko Gvardiol winner handed Enzo Maresca a 2-1 win in his first Premier League game in charge of City against Bournemouth and Liverpool also left it late to draw 2-2 with Newcastle.

Arsenal's opening win was far more straightforward, swatting aside Coventry City 3-0 with minimal fuss. With only one week gone, the Gunners are already odds-on with bookmakers to win the Premier League despite there being 37 games to go.
And Neville is struggling to see a situation where City or Liverpool challenge Arsenal this season.
